data.one_liner: Manage multiple themes, dark mode, and theme persistence in Flutter applications.
data.what_it_does: It provides a ThemeManager, ThemeBuilder widget, and ThemeService to easily swap between multiple ThemeData configurations or toggle light and dark modes. It handles theme persistence using shared_preferences and includes status bar color updates.
use_when: You need to manage more than just a simple light and dark theme (multiple themes)
You want automatic persistence of the user's selected theme across app restarts
You are using the Stacked architecture and want a ThemeService for your view models
avoid_when: you prefer using Riverpod or Bloc for all state management including themes
You only need standard Flutter ThemeMode toggling without extra utilities
strengths: Supports multiple themes beyond just light and dark
Includes business logic access via ThemeService for ViewModels
weaknesses: Tied to the Stacked ecosystem conventions
Adds several third-party dependencies for what can be done natively
data.setup_notes: Awaiting ThemeManager.initialise() in main function before running the app.
